rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Knowing New York City quite well, I would assume I am standing in a most familiar part of New York City and let it surround me.
context_before: that is now something on the surface of the mind ‘out there,’ 3,000 miles away. Standing here, I must shut out the belief that I am in San Francisco.

I came back here. I have done it. I have entered into the state of my desire and I will move across a bridge of incidents, a series of events that will lead me and compel me to take a journey to New York City.

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Neville: My dear, we have eaten of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
context_before: Q. [Inaudible]
context_after: We have enormous pressures in the world to make the world good. We will never bring about an unbalance of good and evil. It is always borne on this tree. This is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and it bears equal number of fruit. So, they have all the efforts in the world to make it a better world. They are up the wrong tree. We�ll get off this tree of good and evil one day and eat of the tree of life [when] that day comes which comes with the resurrection. And the resurrection is not a collective thing; it is an individual experience. We are called out of this state one by one by one, to unite into a single body, who is the risen Lord. So, everyone is favored.
